7.1 Lines, angles and angle facts
Name the relationship first: straight line, full turn, vertically opposite or right angle.
An angle measures a turn. A half-turn along a straight line is 180°, so adjacent angles on a straight
line are supplementary. A full turn about a point is 360°. When two straight lines cross, vertically
opposite angles are equal.

Key idea
Straight line: 180°. Full turn: 360°. Vertically opposite: equal. Right angle: 90°. Complementary
angles sum to 90°; supplementary angles sum to 180°. The middle letter of angle ABC names the
vertex B.
COMMON ERROR
Do not swap the totals: a straight line is 180°, a full turn is 360°. Do not treat vertically opposite
angles as supplementary; they are equal. The adjacent pair is supplementary.

Missing angle on a straight line
PROBLEM
Two adjacent angles on a straight line are 47° and x. Find x.
VISUAL REPRESENTATION
47°
x
A
B
Figure 7.1 · The two angles share a vertex and lie on a straight line.
MATHEMATICAL REASONING
A straight line is a half-turn, so adjacent angles on it are supplementary: their sum is 180°.
STEP-BY-STEP SOLUTION
1. Identify the relationship: the two angles lie on one straight line.
2. Write the equation: 47° + x = 180°.
3. Subtract 47° from both sides: x = 180° − 47° = 133°.
4. Check: 47° + 133° = 180°.
Final answer. x = 133°.
Interpretation. The unknown angle is obtuse. The diagram and the equation agree: the two angles
complete a half-turn.

MATHEMATICAL REASONING
A full turn around a point is 360°. The four angles must fill the turn exactly.
STEP-BY-STEP SOLUTION
1. Add the known angles: 95° + 120° + 85° = 300°.
2. Subtract from the full turn: x = 360° − 300° = 60°.
3. Check: 95° + 120° + 85° + 60° = 360°.
Final answer. x = 60°.
Interpretation. The missing sector is acute. The visual model shows why the total must be 360°, not 180°.

Vertically opposite angles with algebra
PROBLEM
Two lines cross. Vertically opposite angles are labelled 3x + 10° and x + 50°. Find x and one
adjacent angle.
VISUAL REPRESENTATION
3x+10°
x+50°
Figure 7.3 · Opposite angles are equal; adjacent angles sum to 180°.
MATHEMATICAL REASONING
Vertically opposite angles are equal. Adjacent angles on a straight line are supplementary.
STEP-BY-STEP SOLUTION
1. Set the opposite angles equal: 3x + 10 = x + 50.
2. Collect terms: 2x = 40, so x = 20°.
3. Each marked angle is 3(20) + 10 = 70°.
4. An adjacent angle is 180° − 70° = 110°. Check: 70° + 110° = 180°.
Final answer. x = 20°; marked angles 70°; adjacent angle 110°.
Interpretation. The algebra confirms the visual symmetry: opposite sectors match, and neighbouring
sectors complete a line.

Key idea
Corresponding angles sit in the same position at each intersection. Alternate angles lie on
opposite sides of the transversal between the parallel lines. Co-interior angles lie on the same
side between the parallel lines.
WATCH FOR THIS MISCONCEPTION
Do not assume lines are parallel or angles equal unless marked or stated. Conversely, equal
alternate angles or supplementary co-interior angles can show that two lines are parallel.

Key idea
Triangles may be classified by sides (equilateral, isosceles, scalene) and by angles (acute, right,
obtuse). In an isosceles triangle the angles opposite the equal sides are equal; conversely, equal
angles face equal sides. In a right triangle the two acute angles are complementary.
COMMON ERROR
The exterior angle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles. It is not added to
them to make 180°. The adjacent interior angle is the one supplementary to the exterior angle.

PROBLEM
Lines l and m are parallel. The marked angle is 68°. Find a, b and c.
VISUAL REPRESENTATION
l

Figure 7.5 · Parallel marks justify the angle relationships.
MATHEMATICAL REASONING
With parallel lines, alternate angles are equal, co-interior angles are supplementary, and
corresponding angles are equal.
STEP-BY-STEP SOLUTION
1. a is alternate to 68°, so a = 68°.
2. b is co-interior with 68°, so b = 180° − 68° = 112°.
3. c corresponds to the 68° angle (both are in the lower-right position), so c = 68°.
4. Check: a + b = 68° + 112° = 180°.
Final answer. a = 68°, b = 112°, c = 68°.
Interpretation. The transversal creates two angle families: 68° and 112°. Naming the relationship
prevents guessing from appearance.
